question.text: The electric field in a region is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>E</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><msub><mi mathvariant="italic">E</mi><mn mathvariant="italic">0</mn></msub><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><msub><mi mathvariant="italic">E</mi><mn mathvariant="italic">0</mn></msub><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The flux of this field through a rectangular surface, area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> parallel to the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>Z</mi></math> plane is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
